author: as-suvorov
title: JS API E2E Electron cleanup fails on Windows - Permission denied removing d3dcompiler_47.dll
signature: rm cannot remove electron.exe Permission denied|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: JS API (24)
failed_jobs.symptom: E2E Electron test after-all hook fails with 'rm -rf demo-electron-app-project' Permission denied on d3dcompiler_47.dll

root_cause: After the Electron E2E tests complete on Windows, the test cleanup hook attempts to remove the demo-electron-app-project directory using 'rm -rf'. The Electron runner process (or antivirus/Windows file system) holds a lock on the DLL (d3dcompiler_47.dll) preventing deletion. This is a well-known Windows runner flaky issue with Electron test cleanups. The actual test passed; only the teardown failed.
reproduction_steps: N/A — Windows-specific file locking race condition in CI runner environment.
recommended_actions: Re-add PR to the merge queue — the failure is in cleanup only, actual tests passed.
Investigate using 'rimraf' or 'rimraf --glob' in the test teardown to handle locked files on Windows.
Consider adding a retry or force-remove step in the E2E test teardown on Windows.
prevention_strategies: Use a Windows-compatible cleanup utility in the JS API E2E test teardown that handles locked files gracefully (e.g., rimraf with retries).
historical_context: This exact pattern has been seen 15 times (first on 2026-07-09). It consistently occurs in the JS API Windows E2E Electron tests where Electron DLLs remain locked after test run.
